title: Political Chats (Developments Regarding the International Conflicts)
text:
Political Chats

(Answers to Queries Received from Some of the Youth)

1- The questioner says: Is it possible for an agreement like the Kennedy-Khrushchev agreement of 1961 to be concluded, which America would conclude with China? Can we say this? Especially as China, as a global economic power, has become the number one threat to the power of the United States? And then what is the relation of America's threatening of China over Taiwan to that? The answer is that the conclusion of such an agreement is unlikely. Rather, America is working to entangle China in a war with Taiwan so that it can contain it and make it submit to its will, and also to prevent it from supporting Russia in Ukraine. So it carries out actions by which it provokes China, forms alliances around it to work against it, and imposes sanctions on it. And it has launched an economic war against it. Therefore it appears that it will continue these actions until the issue of Taiwan ends in one way or another, because China insists on annexing Taiwan to itself, even by force, as stated by its president Xi Jinping, who was renewed for a third presidential term of five years, when he said: "China will not renounce the right to use force with Taiwan as a last resort and in extreme circumstances" (Al Jazeera, 16/10/2022). And China is watching what is happening in Ukraine and what matters will lead to, so that the tragedy is not repeated with it if Russia is exposed to a crushing defeat in Ukraine. We have seen it refrain from supporting Russia in Ukraine; indeed it backed down after it had announced at the beginning its support for Russia to the furthest limits and signed an agreement with it on this matter, then it stood in a neutral position. This position harmed Russia, and Putin described it as a balanced position, showing understanding of China's position so as not to lose it if he were to reproach or criticise it. Therefore it is probable that America will not conclude with it an agreement of international division, as it did with the Soviet Union previously, until it has exhausted all these actions; and likewise it will not conclude an agreement with it to acknowledge its sphere of influence in the region of the South and East China Sea, for it is mobilising states against it and working to prevent it from controlling these two regions...

2- The questioner says: (Russia could have responded "like the Cuban missile crisis" by threatening the United States in its proximity, as the Soviet Union did previously... So why did it not do so?) The answer to that is that this statement is not realistic with regard to Russia, which feels and acknowledges that America is stronger than it, and this is unlike the Soviet Union, whose power was parallel to American power. To go deeper into these meanings: the nuclear power of the two countries today is almost equal, but America possesses a missile shield that protects it from Russia's missiles, and Russia does not possess such a shield. And what Russia has announced of manufacturing new missiles capable of bypassing the missile shield is still in its early stages, meaning that the number of Russia's nuclear missiles that can reach American territory and bypass the missile shield is small in actual service. In contrast, all of America's old missiles installed to reach Russian territory can still do so. This is in addition to the tremendous advancement in American conventional weapons such as drones, stealth planes and smart munitions, of which Russia possesses nothing comparably close. For the Ukrainian war has proven that the Russian air force is weak and cannot even control the skies of a country like Ukraine, and its drones are backward, and reports speak of its use of Iranian drones in the Ukraine war, as well as other major weaknesses of Russia's conventional forces which the war in Ukraine has exposed, and it has exposed its delusions of greatness. So what kind of great power is it that cannot, in about eight months, defeat a small state like Ukraine, even if it received Western support?! And what greatness does Russia have, which hastened to withdraw from around the capital Kyiv at the beginning of the war, before Western support for Ukraine increased?! That is, when Ukraine was less powerful! Therefore, as I said earlier, the statement (Russia could have responded "like the Cuban missile crisis" by threatening the United States in its proximity) is not realistic, for Russia today is not the Soviet Union of those days at the time of the Cuban missile crisis...

3- As for the issue of international partnership mentioned in the question, for the Americans it means that the major states serve America's interests in return for America's agreement to give them something, decided by America, of the international spoils. For example, Russia agreed to serve America's interests in Syria, so there was its military intervention in 2015, and Russia emerged as a major state, and the Russian "veto" in the Security Council became renowned, and this is an international spoil not to be underestimated. Then America wanted to transfer the Russian services to America to the China basin, against North Korea and against China, but Russia refused. When America became certain of Russia's refusal, America began to diminish Russia's role, which had appeared dominant in Syria, and to harass it in many issues such as the war of Azerbaijan and Armenia and many other matters. This is the American thinking: Washington does not think of sharing influence with anyone; rather, it thinks of involving other states that are called major alongside it, to help it achieve American interests around the world in return for some international spoils which America agrees to grant to this or that state. This is the American thinking with China, with Russia and with the European states. Part of it today is that America is expanding Germany's role in Eastern Europe in confronting Russia, but all of that under the supervision and planning of the American leadership; and if Germany decided to depart from the American leadership and its planning and to act alone, America would begin harassing it... This is the logic that prevails in American thinking...

4- As for the statement mentioned in the question, "Why did the United States not impose sanctions on India when it agreed to import oil from Russia?", the answer to that is that America did not impose sanctions on India because that would threaten the fate of its agents in India led by Modi and his party, the Bharatiya Janata Party. So it did not oppose its purchase of gas and oil from Russia, because it cannot provide it with an alternative. If India stopped its purchase of energy resources from Russia, as happened in Germany, prices would multiply in India, and this is what the people in India cannot bear, and it would be liable to affect the pro-American Modi government and consequently topple it, which is the opportunity awaited by the agents of the British in the Indian Congress Party, who are still strong in India. It even allows it to continue buying weapons from Russia, as has been customary since the era of the Congress Party, which ruled India for most of the periods from its founding in 1947 until 1998. Then the Bharatiya Janata Party came for the first time and ruled until 2004, and then the Congress Party returned to rule India until 2014, and after that the Bharatiya Janata Party returned to power until today. Its success was at the expense of concessions by the agent rulers of Pakistan, as America ordered them, especially in Kashmir, which strengthened the popularity of this party. Therefore, when India bought S-400 missiles from Russia, America did not impose sanctions on it as it imposed them on Turkey; rather, it exempted India from sanctions under the Countering America's Adversaries Through Sanctions Act, known by the abbreviation "CAATSA", as the US House of Representatives approved the exemption as part of its approval of the US defence budget for 2023 on 14/7/2022, on the claim that "the exemption from sanctions will strengthen the defence ties between the United States and India" (Anadolu, 16/7/2022). This was considered a blatant double standard, as sanctions were imposed on Turkey for this reason under this law and were not imposed on India. This indicates that America fears losing its influence in India through the fall of its agents in the Bharatiya Janata Party if it imposed such sanctions on it and it were prevented from buying energy resources from Russia. Whereas that does not affect Erdogan and his government, which revolves in its orbit; rather, it increases his popularity and covers up his ties with America.

5- As for the other points mentioned in the queries about oil and gas, the response to them is as follows:

a- Europe is the number one party harmed by the cutting of the Russian energy supply chains. That is because Europe sees the dangers of Russia's expansion close to it, so it wants, in agreement with America, to be more capable of confronting Russia when it is not dependent on its gas and oil, and it is prepared to bear the consequences. Therefore it is not said that America is directing Europe to rid itself of dependence on Russian energy, even though this American orientation is an old-new American strategy. Rather, it can be said that America succeeded, by hardening Ukraine's positions, supporting it and drawing it towards the West, in entangling Russia in Ukraine. That is, it will have succeeded, through decades of intervention in Ukraine, in cornering Russia in this corner, which cannot be understood except as a threat to the whole of Europe. And when Russia's threat to Europe became present and real, the European states were willingly carried along with the American strategy, and consequently Russian energy resources were cut off from Europe. This was followed by a rise in natural gas prices, as this gas used to come to it through many pipelines and not by sea tankers that transport liquefied gas, and therefore it was cheap. When those pipelines were "cut off", it became necessary for it to import it mostly by sea tankers, and this is costly because of the industry of liquefying gas in the exporting states and then returning it to the gaseous state in the importing states in Europe.

b- As for oil, its prices rose globally and not only in Europe, unlike gas, for America too was harmed by the rise in the price of oil. The same can be said about grain, whose Russian and Ukrainian source was disrupted, meaning that the rise in grain prices was also global and not only European. In Europe, as in the rest of the world, the issue of the shortage of grain and the shortage of oil is an issue of rising prices, because of the possibility of transporting it from regions other than Russia and Ukraine. As for natural gas, it is otherwise, because of the newness of the gas liquefaction industry and the relative scarcity of gas tankers. Also contributing to this was the world's increased dependence on natural gas, for reasons that have been promoted over decades relating to the environment and the climate, that is, that it is less polluting and less dangerous than others such as coal and nuclear energy.

c- As for America dreaming of pricing natural gas internationally in dollars, this is certain, but there are great obstacles in front of it. Russia is agreeing with China and with other states on trade exchange in local currencies, and this is a Russian approach that has made its way since 2014. Indeed, many states have been thinking of the like of it since the financial crisis of 2009, when the states of the world discovered the severity of their dependence on America's dollar. It can be said that the approach of trade exchange in other than the dollar has indeed made its way in the world, even if it is still limited. Perhaps America's raising of interest rates and the new strong-dollar policy that it began to pursue in 2022 are something by which America wants to restore confidence in the dollar and to weaken that approach of trade exchange in other local currencies. In the long term, climate policies lead to more dependence on natural gas internationally and to an increase in the importance of this energy source, and consequently the issue of pricing it in dollars would be of great benefit to America...

d- It may be more important to view the success of America's efforts to cut the gas supply chains between Russia and Europe through pipelines, such as the Nord Stream lines, as a cutting of energy lines that are not controlled by America. What indicates this is that America did not pressure Turkey to cut the gas lines with Russia, considering that Turkey is one of America's dependents. So Russia's President Putin announced intentions to establish a Turkish hub for supplying Russian gas to Europe, meaning that America wants the trade of Russian gas to Europe in the future to be through routes that Washington controls.

6th of Rabi' al-Akhir 1444 AH

31/10/2022 CE
